Tosafot on Bava Batra 123b:6:1.hebrew: היתה מוחכרת או מושכרת ביד אחרים בכור נוטל פי שנים - לקמן מוקי לה כרבי, דלרבנן אין הבכור נוטל פי שנים בשבח ששבחו נכסים לאחר מיתת אביהן. אע"ג דבכור ופשוט שהניח להן אביהן עבד או בהמה טמאה — עובד לזה יום אחד ולזה שני ימים, ה"נ אי אמר הבכור: "או תחלקו, או אטול פי שנים בשבח" — הרשות בידו. והא דלא נקט "חכרוה ושכרוה היתומין" — משום דהשתא אשמעינן חידוש טפי, דאע"ג שהיתה חכורה ושכורה בחיי האב, לא חשבינן להפרה ראוי ויטול פי שנים:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 123b:6:1.english: If it was leased or rented out to others, the firstborn takes a double portion - Below (the Gemara) establishes this according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], for according to the Rabbis, the firstborn does not take a double portion in the appreciation that the property gained after their father's death. Even though in the case of a firstborn and an ordinary heir whose father left them a slave or an unclean animal, [the slave] works one day for this one and two days for that one, so too here, if the firstborn said, "Either divide [the property], or I will take a double portion in the appreciation," the choice is in his hands. And as for the fact that [the Baraita] did not say, "the orphans leased it or rented it" — [this is] because now it teaches us a greater novelty: that even though it was leased and rented out during the father's lifetime, we do not consider the cow as [property] that is "ready" [to be inherited], and [the firstborn] takes a double portion.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 123b:8:1.hebrew: הכא במכירי כהונה (ולויה) עסקינן - בכל דוכתא עביד מכירי כהונה מוחזק. בפרק כל הגט (גיטין דף ל.): המלוה מעות את הכהן והלוי. והיינו טעמא, שזהו מתנה מועטת, ואסור לחזור בו, ואפי' בדברי' בעלמא. ואע"פ שאם רצה יכול לחזור בו, מכל מקום כל כמה דלא הדר הוי כמוחזק. ודוקא דאשתחיט בחיי אבוהון; הא לאו הכי — לא, כיון דמת, מי יזכה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 123b:8:1.english: Here we are dealing with those who are acquainted with a priesthood (and Levite) - In every place [the Gemara] treats those acquainted with a priest as having an established [claim]. In the chapter Kol HaGet (Gittin 30a): One who lends money to a priest or a Levite [may repay himself with the priestly or Levitical gifts]. And this is the reason: because this is a minor gift, and it is forbidden to retract from it, even through words alone. And although, if he wished, he could retract from it, nevertheless, so long as he has not retracted, it is considered as established. And this applies specifically where [the animal] was slaughtered during their father's lifetime; but if not, then no — since [the father] died, who would [be the one to] acquire it?

Tosafot on Bava Batra 123b:8:2.english: And he holds that gifts that have not been separated are considered as though they have been separated - This is puzzling, for shortly afterward [the Gemara] establishes it according to Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi], and at the end of the second chapter of Kiddushin (58a) he holds that [such gifts] are not considered as though they have been separated. And one can answer that the Tanna here does not agree with Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] except in this matter, that a firstborn takes a double portion in an improvement [in value of the estate]. Alternatively, it is only with regard to the gifts of terumat ma'aser (the terumah separated from the tithe) that Rabbi holds that they are not considered as though they have been separated, but the gifts here, the foreleg and the jaw, which are recognizable, he holds that they are considered as though they have been separated:
